# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

Stats: 4 obs (1,712t read) | 29,814t work | 94% savings

### Nov 3, 2026
5 1:35a ○ ms package unit parsing structure mapped for adding microseconds
6 " ◆ Microsecond unit added to ms parsing, types, README, and tests
7 " ○ Uppercase micro sign breaks StringValue typing for µS input
8 " ● Uppercase micro sign type error resolved by adding 'µS' to UnitAnyCase
S3 Add microsecond support to ms: ms('500us') returns 0.5, accepting µs, microsecond and microseconds in any case; update types, README and tests (Nov 3, 1:36 AM)
**Investigated**: The ms repository layout, src/index.ts unit definitions, parse regex and switch, README unit documentation, and the existing millisecond tests in index.test.ts, parse.test.ts and parse-strict.test.ts.

**Learned**: Units are defined as millisecond multiples, and parsing uses a case-insensitive regex plus an exhaustive switch, so new units must be added to the Unit union, the regex and the switch. Uppercase<'µs'> yields a Greek capital mu rather than the micro sign, so the uppercase micro sign form needs an explicit type entry. The runtime normalizes Greek mu (U+03BC) to micro sign (U+00B5) after lowercasing.

**Completed**: Added Microseconds to the Unit type and the parse regex, with a switch branch that divides by 1000. ms('500µs') returns 0.5, and parse and parseStrict accept the same forms. Added 'µS' to UnitAnyCase so the uppercase form type-checks. Updated the README type listing and examples. Added microsecond tests to all three test files. Typecheck, biome lint and jest all pass (170 tests, 100% coverage). Changes are uncommitted.

**Next Steps**: Awaiting user direction. Open questions are whether to add plain 'us', and whether microsecond output formatting (format()) is wanted; neither is implemented.

**Notes**: format(0.5) still returns "0.5ms", so microsecond output is not supported. The microsecond type alias and its TS entries were added to support both micro sign and Greek mu inputs, which is a deliberate design choice worth reviewing.
